editorial:
Imagine landing your dream job at a fancy consulting firm in Paris, only to find out your first big project is basically a hit list for employees. That is exactly what happens to Philippe. You get to see him struggle between his hunger for success and his basic human feelings. The vibe is very tense and cold, showing you the world of high-stakes business where people are just numbers on a spreadsheet. You will feel the pressure he is under as his girlfriend calls him out for helping a greedy system, making you wonder if you would do the same thing to get ahead in your career.

The acting is solid and keeps you grounded in the drama, though the pacing can feel a bit slow at times because it focuses more on talking than action. If you like movies that make you think about right and wrong, you will love this. It is a great pick for a quiet night in. You should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you can rent it on Apple TV if you want something quick. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: By the end, you see Philippe face the reality of his choices. He realizes that the corporate world does not care about him any more than he cared about the workers. After causing so much pain to the factory staff, he finds himself trapped in the same cold system he helped build. The movie wraps up with a sad realization that chasing money and power often leaves you feeling empty and alone in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about office politics and moral dilemmas.
